 J U D G M E N T
This petition Under section 166 MV act is filed seeking compensation of Rs.8,00,000/ for the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. It is stated that on 17092019 about 12.25 a.m.,(mid night) petitioner and other 3 people were helping to one Mr.Chandra, who was fell down on the road with his bolero vehicle, due to heavy rain, opposite to HP Petrol Bunk on B.M.Road, near Janapada Loka, the driver of Goods Carrier bearing No.KA01 AG1607 (herein after called as offending vehicle) drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the Bolero vehicle, petitioner and other 3 members.
Due to the impact, petitioner and other 3 members sustained severe injuries.

Immediately, he was taken to Govt. Hospital, Ramanagara, from there he was shifted to R.R.Hospital and then he was referred to Nimhans hospital, Bengaluru for head injury, after taking necessary treatment, he was shifted to Victoria hospital, due to inconvenience, he was discharged and admitted to Vijaya hospital for further treatment, wherein he has taken treatment as an inpatient for 5 days.
After discharge, till now he is under treatment as an outpatient.
It is submitted that the petitioner has spent huge amount towards his treatment, medicines, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental expenses.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is suffering from permanent disability and unable to lead normal life as earlier.

It is claimed that petitioner was working as an attender at Innovative School,
Ramasandra and was earning Rs.15,000/ p.m.
Due to accidental injuries he has lost his earning capacity and lost his income.

As the accident was caused due to negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle, it is requested to award compensation from the respondent No.1 to 3 being the insurer and RC owners of offending vehicle.
3. In response to the petition notice, respondent No.1 has appeared before the court through its counsel and filed its written statement.
Respondent No.2 and 3 have not appeared before the court and they were placed exparte.
4. The first RespondentInsurance company has filed its written statement denying the entire averments of the petition.
It has admitted the issuance of policy and its validity as on the date of accident.
Further it has contended that the owner of the offending vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
Further it is contended that the petition is bad for nonjoinder of necessary party as the owner and insurer of car bearing No.KA09B4705 were not made as parties to this petition.

It has denied the age,

sentences.text: It has contended that the accident has occurred due to negligence of petitioner himself as he was walking and standing on the middle of the road without observing moving vehicles and there was no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
Further, the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid DL.
For all these reasons, this respondent prayed for dismissal of the petition.

5. In order to prove the claim, the petitioner is examined as PW1 and Medical Record Keeper is examined as PW2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.17.
6.
The first Respondent has examined the SDA, RTO, Bengaluru (Central) as RW1 and got marked 3 documents at Ex.R1 to 3.
Further it has examined the SDA, RTO, Bengaluru North as RW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.R.4 and 5.

The official of Respondent No.1 is also examined as RW3 and got marked the documents at Ex.R6 to 8.
7.
I have heard the counsel for petitioner and perused the material on record.
8. On the basis of the above, the following Issues were framed :-

1 . Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries along with the other public on 17092019 at 00.25 a.m. helping the person who had fallen on the road along with Bolero vehicle due to heavy rain at opposite to Petrol Bunk on B M Road, near Janapada Loka, only due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of goods carrier bearing No.KA01 AG1607?
2. What compensation petitioner is entitled?
3. What order?
9. By considering the evidences, arguments and the other materials available on record, I have answered the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
R E A S O N S 10.
Issue NO.1:
In order to prove his claim, petitioner relied on the police and medical records.
PW1 is the injured and the direct witness to the incident.

He has deposed that on 17092019 about 12.25 a.m., (mid night) himself and other 3 people were helping to one Mr.Chandra, who was fell down on the road with his bolero vehicle, due to heavy rain opposite to HP Petrol Bunk on B.M.Road, near Janapada Loka, the driver of Goods Carrier bearing No.KA01AG1607 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to him, the Bolero vehicle and other 3 members.

Raju V vs The Manager on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/1509918/
3
Due to the impact, he has sustained severe injuries.
It is stated that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.

11. In support of his claim he has produced copy of FIR and complaint at Ex.P1, statement at Ex.P2,
Crime Details Form with property list sent to Magistrate at Ex.P3, spot sketch at Ex.P4, IMV report at Ex.P5, charge sheet Ex.P6 and wound certificate at Ex.P.7.

As per wound certificate, he has sustained the following injuries:
1. Abrasion 4cm x 1cm present over mid of forehead.
2. Lacerated wound 2 in number measuring 2cm x 0.1cm x 0.2cm and 4cm x 0.1 cm x 0.2cm present over outer aspect of left eye.
3. Abraded laceration wound covering an area of 8cm x 4cm present over outer aspect of left foot.
4. Lacerated wound 1cm x 0.5cm x 1cm present over dorsum of left foot.
5. CT brain reveals fracture of left temporal bone, roof of left orbit(eyesocket)
6. CT brain reveals subdural hemorrhage of right parietal bone.
The doctor opined that the injuries No.1 to 4 are simple in nature and injuries No.5 and 6 are grievous in nature.
12. According to the petitioner he was helping the person who had fell down along with his Bolero vehicle due to rain.
It is said that one Bolero vehicle bearing No.KA 01B4705 had fell down and a person by name Chandra was seeking help.
Petitioner and others were helping him and at the same time, the offending vehicle came in high speed and hit them causing injuries.
Respondent Insurance company has contended that it was the negligence on the part of the driver of the Bolero vehicle who did not take any measures to caution other vehicles passing on the road.
It is contended that the RC owner and the insurer of Bolero vehicle are necessary parties to the petition.
PW1 in his crossexamination has admitted that Bolero vehicle is responsible for the accident as he stopped his vehicle only on the request of driver of Bolero vehicle.
The petitioner had admitted the suggestion and said that Bolero vehicle was responsible.
Based on this statement only Insurance company wanted to implead RC owner and insurer of Bolero vehicle to the petition, but the same was rejected by this tribunal.
As it could be seen that the Bolero vehicle got skid and fallen on the road and after seeing the same, petitioner and his friends stopped their car and went to help him.
In such a situation, driver of the Bolero could not be expected to take precautionary measures or put any indicator for other vehicles.
Petitioner had said that they were standing on the road and directing the other vehicles to move carefully.
While doing so he and his friends were hit by the offending vehicle.
It cannot be said that negligence was of the driver of the Bolero vehicle or the petitioner who went to help them.
Since the offending vehicle was in high speed it did not control and stop over there or to move without hitting the petitioner and others.

sentences.text: The police after investigation have filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle and all the other available records indicates the negligence of him only.
The evidence of PW 1 corroborates with the documents produced by him.
There is nothing elicited to disprove the negligence on the part of the offending vehicle.
From all the above documents it is clear that the petitioner sustained injuries in road traffic accident that occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.
Hence, issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
14. ISSUE NO.2 : As it is held in Issue No.1 that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle, the petitioner is entitled to get compensation.

15. So far as the quantum of compensation is concerned, the petitioner has sought for compensation of Rs.8,00,000/ for the injuries sustained by him in road traffic accident and submitted that he has spent more than Rs.1,10,000/ towards treatment, nourishment, conveyance and other charges.
The petitioner has produced 29 medical bills at Ex.P12 for Rs.87,941/ to show the expenses incurred by him.

The Ex.P.10 discharge summary shows that petitioner has sustained Head injury right temporal and right parietal haemorrhagic contusion and he was treated with wound debridement and skin grafting over left ankle joint and left eye and he was treated as an inpatient in Vijaya hospital from 17092019 to 21092019.
So also, there are no evidence that the petitioner has sustained any disability as he has not examined the doctor.
The petitioner has examined the Medical record keeper of Vijaya Hospital as PW2, who has produced the case sheet belongs to the petitioner.
There are no evidences that the petitioner is suffering from any difficulties which would affect his livelihood and daytoday activities and earning capacity.
The injuries do not appear to be much grievous causing disability to the petitioner.
In the cross examination of PW1 has stated that he has left the job as he is unable to work now.
However, as discussed earlier absolutely there are no materials to show loss of earning capacity to the petitioner.
In the absence of medical evidence to prove disability, I deem it proper to award global compensation.
16. The petitioner says that he is aged about 32 years at the time of accident and due to the accident he had to suffer a lot.
As per wound certificate he has sustained simple as well as grievous injuries.
He has produced medical bills for Rs.87,941/ and taken treatment as an inpatient for a period of 5 days.
By considering the nature of injuries, 5 days admission in the hospital and considering the pain and sufferings by the petitioner, I think this would be a proper case to award global compensation.

Considering, 5 days admission in the hospital and nature of injuries sustained and on perusal of medical bills, I deem it appropriate to award Rs.2,50,000/ as global compensation under all the conventional heads with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
17. Liability:
The respondentinsurance company has denied its liability on the ground that the offending vehicle had no valid permit as on the date of accident.
Insurance company examined officials from RTO Bengaluru Central and RTO Bengaluru North as RW1 and 2 respectively.
Permit and registration details, permit copy of the offending vehicle are produced at Ex.R.2, Ex.R.3 and 5 respectively.
According to these records, the permit of the offending vehicle was cancelled on 178 2018 since the vehicle was migrated from RTO Bengaluru Central to RTO Bengaluru North on 28 082019.
RW2 says that as on the date of accident i.e. on 17 092019, the offending vehicle did not possess valid permit.
From the records, it is found that the vehicle was of 2016 model and RW2 Raju V vs The Manager on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/1509918/

sentences.text: 5 admits that the permit will be valid for 5 years generally from the date of registration.
Hence, it is argued by the petitioner that till 2021 the vehicle had permit and due to change of ownership it was cancelled temporarily till it get registered with the other RTO.
He denied the suggestion that there will be a grace period of 30 days to get the permit or to renew it.
It appears that since the ownership was changed the permit was cancelled.
However, the RC owner was not authorized to ply the vehicle without obtaining fresh permit.
Subsequently the vehicle was again registered and permit was valid from 23102019 to 22102024.
The accident has occurred between the period of migration from RTO to the other.
RC owner should have taken care and should not have plied the vehicle on road without permit.

18. Since plying of vehicle without valid registration and permit has been held to be fundamental breach of conditions in Narinder Singh v. New India Assurance Company Limited, (2014) 9 SCC 324, therefore, Insurance Company would be entitled for application of principle of Pay & Recover from insured as it has been held in catena of judgments including recent ones in Shamanna v.
Divisional Manager, Oriental Insurance Company Limited, reported in (2018) 9 SCC 650.
19.

sentences.text: In view of the above observation, the Respondent No.3 RC owner of the offending vehicle is held liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Since the Insurance policy was in the name of second Respondent, he is a proper party and the insurance company is liable to indemnify even if the policy is not transferred in the name of new owner.

As it is a third party liability, the First respondent Insurance Company is directed to satisfy the award in the first instance & pay it to the claimant, where after it is liable get reimbursed the same from the owner, in accordance with law.
Hence, the insurance company shall pay the compensation to the petitioner with interest @ 6% p.a.
With these observation I answer Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
20. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issues No.1 &
2, I proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is allowed in part with cost.

Petitioner is awarded  compensation of Rs.2,50,000/
together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit with the Tribunal.
Respondent No.3 is held liable to pay the aforesaid amount to the petitioner.

Respondent No.1 shall deposit aforesaid amount within three months from the date of this Order and recover the entire compensation amount along with interest from the respondent No.3owner in view of violation of terms of insurance contract.
The entire compensation amount shall be disbursed to the petitioner through Epayment on proper identification.

Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
